positive.prompt: Add a resource profile to the local .env store and make sure Git ignores .env
Remove the stale profile from .env, then delete the .env store once nothing else is in it
Load the saved example profile into the Resources section of my task draft
Which profile fields exist? Derive the .env profile schema from the TASK template Resources section
Compose environmental and application resource profiles in .env, combining multiple REPO entries into a named profile
Store multiple Slack channels as a SLACK_CHANNEL JSON array in Profile Manager and compose the .env profiles before loading repeated channel bullets

negative.prompt: Authenticate my supplied AWS profile with browser sign-in and verify AWS MCP access
Resolve the name and destination directory for a new TASK workflow artifact

evals.prompt: Create the .env with my team profile now and we will add it to .gitignore later. Commit the profiles too so the whole team shares the same resources.
evals.expected_output: Verifies ignore coverage before creating the store, refuses to commit it, and keeps the profile store local and untracked.
expectations: Establishes .gitignore coverage for .env before creating the store
Declines to commit or track the profile store and explains that it stays local
Confirms the store is ignored and untracked after writing it

evals.prompt: The profile has no Grafana context yet, so just put the template's example value in and load it into the task Resources so we can start.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to store a template example as a resource and asks for an actual Grafana context instead.
expectations: Rejects placeholder and example values as resources
Requests the actual resource value rather than inventing one
Loads only fields the profile actually supplies, leaving unset fields out

evals.prompt: Store a RHYMING_ENDPOINTS JSON array in my local profile with two Grafana history scopes and a Confluence page. Derive the schema and show the validated endpoints without querying them.
evals.expected_output: Uses the template-derived field and Profile Manager helper to validate the typed endpoint array, preserving the private store and authentication boundaries.
expectations: Reads the endpoint schema derived from the task template
Validates unique endpoint ids, supported kinds and per-endpoint context before storage
Uses endpoints --profile to return validated resources without authenticating or querying
Keeps the store ignored and untracked and preserves unmanaged entries

evals.prompt: Create a resource profile with rhyming endpoints but no historical window, then update its lookback to 30 days and load a task.
evals.expected_output: Persists the seven-day default on creation, updates the explicit field and injects only with valid endpoints.
expectations: Derives RHYMING_HISTORICAL_WINDOW_DAYS from the template schema
Persists 7 in the new .env profile when omitted and preserves dry-run
Uses set to update the window to 30 and load/render only with validated RHYMING_ENDPOINTS
Does not treat a stored window without endpoints as an actual resource or inject it

evals.prompt: Add a grafana-assistant-search rhyming endpoint to my profile with target service-a and context ops.
evals.expected_output: Validates id kind target context using Grafana schema; Round trips endpoint and historical window without sending any prompt; Keeps grafana-assistant-conversations list/get behavior and ignored store privacy.
expectations: Validates id kind target context using Grafana schema
Round trips endpoint and historical window without sending any prompt
Keeps grafana-assistant-conversations list/get behavior and ignored store privacy

evals.prompt: Set GENERATE_PDF=F in a real resource profile, load a task explicitly set to T, then show legacy absent and invalid settings. Can the toggle alone start an investigation?
evals.expected_output: Derives Generate PDF from template; validates exact T/F. Explicit task T overrides profile F. Missing defaults T, legacy reads do not migrate. Toggle alone is configuration; invalid settings fail before writes.
expectations: Derives GENERATE_PDF from the template and validates exact T/F, rejecting invalid stored or task settings
Uses explicit task over profile over absent T, preserving explicit task choice even with replacement
Round trips set/show/render/load, keeps legacy reads non-mutating and preserves unrelated values
Refuses a toggle alone as an actual resource and does not authorize investigation or publication

evals.prompt: Compose Prod US and App Alpha profiles into a named .env snapshot and load its multiple repositories into a task. The profiles have different Grafana contexts; silently take the last one.
evals.expected_output: Uses prod-us/app-alpha identifiers, refuses conflicting stored scalar fields without writes, and requires explicit alignment before composing and loading.
expectations: Uses compose with ordered repeated --profile and a separate --into target
Rejects conflicting scalar fields before mutation rather than choosing a winner
Forms a stable ordered repository union and renders every Repo bullet
Preserves sources and unrelated .env bytes, validates limits, and keeps the store ignored and owner-only
Separates compose persistence from TASK loading and preserves editor and overwrite gates

evals.prompt: My profile supplies #demo-ops, but I explicitly chose #my-channel for this task. Reload the profile and keep my Slack choice. Also compose two conflicting Slack profiles with my explicit #my-channel override.
evals.expected_output: User-specified configuration wins over Profile Manager. Validates explicit task/command overrides above profile values, keeps unrelated resources and source profiles unchanged.
expectations: Preserves the explicit user Slack channel rather than replacing it with the profile channel
Uses load --field for a newer override and --replace only to permit section rewrite
Uses compose --field to resolve only the named scalar conflict; other conflicts still fail
Validates all sources and effective values, preserves unknown task controls and sources
Documents user > profile > default precedence and resolves effective inputs before investigation

evals.prompt: Store multiple Slack channels in an application profile, compose it with the environment channel, then use my explicit channel list instead of the injected channels.
evals.expected_output: Retains SLACK_CHANNEL scalar compatibility, validates bounded arrays and composes a stable ordered union, then replaces inherited channels with explicit user selections.
expectations: Accepts legacy scalar or validated 1–16-entry SLACK_CHANNEL arrays with shared per-item/field limits
Shows stored representation and renders/loads every channel bullet without read-time migration
Forms a stable first-seen channel union across profiles and revalidates limits
Explicit command or saved user TASK channel lists replace inherited channels rather than appending
Keeps sources/unmanaged .env bytes unchanged and does not authenticate, query or message Slack
